services.name: Surf and wake
services.desc: Our new exhibition explores the rise and fall (and rise again) of the American Main Street. Over the course of the 20th century, Main Street emerged as more than just a place-it became an emblem of democracy itself, so much so that when Disneyland was constructed in 1955, it centered its park around an ersatz “Main Street USA.” But the postwar rise of the private automobile, suburbanization, and the Urban Renewal movement of the 1960s and 1970s-in which downtowns were gutted and turned into a series of failed malls and parking lots-ushered in a long decline for Main Streets.
